name: An SSH key bound to a principal acts only as that principal's actors
aliases: an actor belongs to a principal
summary: An SSH key can be bound to a principal (a lane, person:NAME). ssh_forced_command.py takes --principal NAME from its own arguments (the authorized_keys line, never the connection) and starts the endpoint with --key-principal NAME. The project's session registry gains an owners map, actor to principal, written only when non-empty so an unconfigured installation keeps today's bytes. On a bound key, endpoint.execute refuses every request whose actor that map does not give to the key's principal, before any action; session register is the exception and records the new actor under the key's principal; session show returns the principal. A key with no --principal reads no owner and behaves as before. admin.py authorized-keys --principal prints the bound contributor line (comment orchestra-principal=person:NAME); adopt-actor PROJECT ACTOR --principal person:NAME --actor OPERATOR --reason TEXT gives an existing actor to a principal once, refuses a name on the operator allowlist that another principal owns in another project, and records it in actor-adoptions.audit.json, which admin.py actor-adoptions prints. Downgrade: a kit that predates this refuses a registry whose owners map is present.
